To protect public health, this meeting is being held in accordance with AB 361, Government
Code section 54954(e)(1) (A). Given the proclaimed state of emergency and the Los Angeles
County Health Department recommendation for social distancing for public meetings, which is
also consistent with Cal OSHA requirements for social distancing, the City will be conducting
public meetings via video/teleconferencing and there will be no physical location available for
this meeting. To participate in the City of Commerce ‘public meetings and provide public
comment during the COVID-19 public health emergency, please follow these steps:

1. Watch or Listen: Meetings are broadcast/streamed live on the City of Commerce’s
Facebook:  https://www.facebook.com/City-of-Commerce-123903054365151/?ref.  Archived,
on-demand video of each meeting is maintained on the City’s Facebook as part of the public
record.

2. Submit Comments before the Meeting: Members of the public can provide public comment
by sending an e-mail to cityclerk@ci.commerce.ca.us for City Council meetings, and the
comment will be read during Public Comment portion.

3. Live Remote Public Comments: Members of the public may submit live public comment via
Zoom conferencing by using the link below. You must download the Zoom app or software.
Zoom meetings can be accessed by telephone, computer, or smart device. You will be allowed
to speak during Public Comment portion of the agenda.

Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Mendoza called meeting to order at 5:08 p.m. via teleconferencing.  

ROLL CALL Councilmember Soria left the meeting at 6:30 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda.  

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council recessed to Closed Session at 5:10 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:44 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: 

Items #1.A, #2, and #3 - the staff made a presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on any of those items.

The City Council did not discuss items #1.B and #4. 

City Attorney Tapia announced that staff is recommending to continue item #12 to a Special City Council meeting on February 15, 2022. 


6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Mendoza called meeting to order at 6:46 p.m. via teleconferencing. 

ROLL CALL

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Sergeant Villareal provided an update for two weeks. Deploying two motor units to help with traffic and in problematic areas. Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo asked for a Neighborhood Watch meeting in the Rosini area due to a recent shooting. Mayor Mendoza suggested a combined Neighborhood watch meeting that would encompass the Rosini area and Rosewood park area. 

PUBLIC COMMENT Rita Villa thanked the City Council for adjourning the meeting in memory of her brother, who passed away. 

Raul Lorenzano introduced himself as a field representative for Assembly Member Christina Garcia. 

Osvaldo Pena introduced himself as a new Gas Company Public Affairs manager. 

Mark from East Side Communities for Environmental Justice spoke in support of item #6. 

Kevin Larsen, President of AFSCME Local 773, asked that the City Council consider bringing furloughed employees back.  




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

5.. Water Replenishment District PFAS Remediation Program Participation Agreement

4.. Weed Abatement - Declaring that Weeds, Brush, Rubbish are a Public Nuisance

8.. Award of Construction Contract for Camp Commerce Pool and Spa Replastering Project and Authorize Measure AA Fund Transfer for Project Cost Shortfall

6.. Resolution Accepting a Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority Open Streets Grant to Help Fund a Temporary Event for Bicyclists and Pedestrians

3.. Re-Ratifying the Proclamation of a State of Emergency by Governor Newsom, and Re-Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the Legislative Bodies of the City of Commerce for the 30-Day Period

7.. Letter of Agreement between the City of Commerce and CCEA related to access to the Senior Center Facility

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 12A, & 12B

PUBLIC HEARING

9.. Substantial Amendment to the 46th and 47th Year of Community Development Block Grant Funds for Fiscal Years 2020/2021 and 2021/2022 and Authorizing the Allocation for the 48th Year of Community Development Block Grant Funds for Fiscal Year 2022/2023  - PUBLIC HEARING  -  Action: amend (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Economic Development and Planning Jimenez provided a brief overview of the staff report.  Discussion took place about Home Preservation Program.  

SCHEDULED MATTERS

11.. City Council Handbook Amendment  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo City Attorney Tapia provided an overview of the staff report.

10.. Adopt Resolution Making Certain Findings and Approving an Energy Services Contract With Alliance Building Solutions  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Manager Cisneros provided an overview of the staff report. There will be no increase in rates. City Manager Cisneros stated that while the maps are updated to reflect more legible graphics, the routes remain the same. 

Mayor Pro Tem, Mayor, and Councilmembers thanked Nationwide for looking for environmental needs and helping the region. This program will provide a better quality of life for residents. Mendoza thanked the company for zero emissions. 


ORDINANCES

13.. First Reading of Uncodified Ordinances Approving Amended and Restated Development Agreements Related to Applications #18-074 and #18-027 and Replacing Commercial Cannabis Development Agreements No. 724 and No. 727  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Planner Knarik Vizcarra provided an overview of the staff report.  

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Altamirano wished Happy Birthday to coach Phillip Briones. 

Councilmember Argumedo wished Happy Birthday to his brother and his son. 

Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo wished her sister a Happy Birthday. Mayor Pro Tem Rebollo issued her condolences to the Villanova family.

Mayor Mendoza asked that the notary services be resumed. On January 28, 2022, mayor Mendoza reported that he attended the City celebration and Lions international, regional meeting. 
Mayor Mendoza asked that the CERT program be initiated, training resumed for the search and rescue team, and also bring back Comcats program. 



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:51 p.m. in memory of Fernando Villanova and Ruben Stephen Aldrete.
